extension.summary: Pick from a list of websites, launch fullscreen in Chrome, and control the mouse with the Kodi remote
extension.description: Shows a menu of configured websites, then launches your choice fullscreen in Chrome (kiosk mode) and lets you move the real Windows mouse cursor and click using Kodi's remote directional buttons. Configure up to 5 sites in addon settings. Windows only.

extension.news:
1.1.2 - Group files stay inside the add-on profile; a malformed JSON group is no longer deleted on read
1.1.1 - Creating a group now refreshes My Groups immediately - Remove Group is on the group context menu (not Edit Group) - Stop forcing a list view (no label sort methods, no default "files" content, programs-only) - Directory listings are not cached, so new groups and shortcuts show up on refresh - Wipe Add-on Data shows a success dialog when it finishes - Tools includes the Settings actions (icon color, context menu, advanced editing, debug logging, backup / restore) - Tools and Settings use the same backup folder
1.1.0 - Fanart re-balanced with a wider left margin so it doesn't compete with the addon browser's overlaid title/description text - Subfolders are now ordered entries within their parent group, alongside regular shortcuts, instead of always being listed separately before them - Shortcuts and subfolders can now be freely reordered relative to each other (previously shortcuts and subfolders could only be reordered within their own separate lists) - New subfolders are appended below existing items by default - Removed the standalone "New Subfolder" menu entry (which also showed up inside home-screen widgets); creating a subfolder is now done via the context menu on any item, matching how everything else is managed - Existing subfolders created by earlier versions are automatically migrated into the new ordering the first time their parent group is opened
1.0.0 - First standalone release of Shortcut Manager, forked from AutoWidget - New, independent add-on ID (plugin.program.shortcutmanager) so this installs cleanly with no pre-existing shortcuts - Shortcuts-only: all Widget functionality and widget caching have been removed - Added support for Shortcut subfolders (nested Shortcut Groups) - New icon, fanart, banner, poster, and clearlogo artwork - Restored a minimal background service solely to keep the "Add to Shortcut Manager Group" context menu setting working (no caching or refresh loop) - Fixed a bug (present since the original AutoWidget) where saving a change while editing a Group's properties would lose track of the edit context on redisplay - Removed remaining dead code (several functions with no callers) and fixed invalid unescaped XML in settings.xml - Provider changed to Bob - Icon now has a fully transparent background; fanart redesigned to match the icon and wordmark

extension.summary: Picture-in-Picture for The Loop via mpv (Windows and Android)
extension.description:
Watch a second stream as Picture-in-Picture while your main stream keeps playing.
PiP utilises MPV, a free, open source, and cross-platform media player.
extension.news:
1.3.9 - Audit fix: _resize_step()'s own docstring still referenced the old 30% default width and its resulting 15% step size, left stale by the 40% default change in 1.3.7 - the code itself was always correct (the step size is always derived live from the current setting), only the example figures in the comment were wrong. Updated to the correct 20% figure. Confirmed via a byte-level diff against the actual shipped 1.3.8 package that this was the only change since - everything else re-verified unchanged
1.3.8 - Fixed a genuine inconsistency: every other cleanup path (a launch failure, the resolve fallback, service.py's automatic health-check for a crashed PiP) already forced Kodi's own GUI back to fullscreen video afterward, but a manual "Close PiP" click never went through any of those, so close_pip() itself never did it. Now does, and the now-redundant duplicate call in service.py's health-check was removed since close_pip() handles it internally - Worth being direct about a separate, unresolved part of the report this was raised alongside: if some other Windows application (e.g. File Explorer) is the current OS-level foreground window, this fix does not necessarily bring Kodi itself above it - ActivateWindow(fullscreenvideo) is a Kodi-internal GUI command affecting what Kodi displays within its own window, not an OS-level window-focus command. Confirmed via Microsoft's own documentation that the relevant Windows API for that (SetForegroundWindow) has real, deliberate restrictions on which processes can use it to steal focus - not something to promise fixes reliably without testing it directly first
1.3.7 - Default PiP width changed from 30% to 40% of screen width (settings default and the Python-side fallback used if the setting is ever unreadable, kept consistent with each other) - Confirmed, not just re-asserted: mpv's own --autofit is documented to act as a bounding box that mpv fits the real video within, without modifying its aspect ratio - the ceiling passed at launch is sized from the width setting, but the actual on-screen shape always follows the real video. Confirmed grow/shrink preserves whatever aspect ratio the window currently has with a direct test across four different real-world shapes (16:9, 4:3, 21:9 ultrawide, and 9:16 vertical/phone) - 16:9 and 4:3 showed exactly zero drift across repeated grow/shrink cycles, and the tiny drift seen in the other two (under 0.004) is expected integer-rounding, not an aspect-ratio bug
1.3.6 - No bugs found this round - genuinely new strategies applied instead of re-reading the same code again: wrote a small custom static analyzer (no internet access in this environment to install a real one) checking for unreachable code, suspicious comparisons, unused locals, bare excepts, and mutable default arguments across every file - found nothing genuine, two apparent hits were confirmed false positives in the analyzer's own crude logic (a return_code == 0 check it mistook for the None-comparison pattern, and three try/except functions where both branches already return explicitly, which its simplistic last-statement check couldn't see into) - Two genuine cleanups from checking whether functions doing similar work computed things identically: the screen height returned by winctl.get_screen_size() was unpacked in _base_size_px() but never used at all (harmless, but untidy) - now only the needed value is unpacked. The current-quadrant calculation in snap_direction() and _resize_from_corner() was duplicated verbatim in both places - extracted into a shared _current_quadrant() helper, tested against multiple positions with results cross-checked against the original formula independently - The Application.SetMute request-build-and-check logic was duplicated nearly identically in start_pip() and swap_audio() - both extracted into a single set_kodi_mute() helper, matching the same pattern already used for get/set_kodi_debug_logging(), tested directly for both the success and Kodi-rejection paths including that the caller-specific context label appears correctly in the log
1.3.5 - Found by systematically searching for a different class of issue this time - multiple related calls where only some results get checked, leaving a genuine partial failure reported as full success. winctl.swap_rects() moved one window successfully and could still silently fail to move the other, while unconditionally reporting the whole swap as successful; now returns success only if both moves genuinely succeeded. Caught and fixed a mistake in my own first attempt at this same fix before shipping it - the initial edit left duplicate, unreachable code from the original function's tail behind, caught by a direct code check afterward rather than assumed clean - The same missed-check pattern also existed in the two calls to mpvipc.set_mute() (mpv's own IPC-based mute, separate from Kodi's own mute, which was fixed in 1.3.3), in start_pip()'s launch-time mute and in swap_audio() - a failure here would leave mpv's own audio out of sync with what Kodi's side was told, with nothing in the log to explain why. Both now check the result and log a warning on failure
1.3.4 - Fixed a real edge case in 1.3.1's fix for the wrong-channel-in-PiP bug, found while re-auditing that exact code and confirmed with a direct reproduction: 1.3.1 only guarded against a later playback event overwriting an ALREADY-correct resolved value. If the PiP target's own resolve genuinely never fires at all - a dead stream, a timeout, a cancelled dialog - the resolved value is still None when the main stream's own resume happens moments later, so that resume's own playback-started event would be wrongly accepted as if it were the PiP target succeeding, launching mpv with the main stream's own channel instead of correctly reporting the resolve as failed. Fixed by explicitly disabling the capture the moment the main stream resume begins, regardless of whether the PiP target's own resolve already succeeded, failed, or never fired at all. Confirmed with a direct reproduction of the exact failure before the fix, and three separate tests afterward covering normal success, a genuinely identical main/PiP channel, and the newly-fixed never-resolves case
1.3.3 - Audit fix: found the same class of issue just fixed in 1.3.2 (a JSON-RPC response discarded without checking for an error) in two more places - the Application.SetMute calls in swap_audio() and in the "PiP starts audible, mute the main stream instead" path of start_pip(). A rejected mute call here is more immediately obvious than the debug-logging case (both streams end up audible), but was still silently unlogged, leaving nothing in the log to explain why if it happened. Both now check the response and log any rejection unconditionally
1.3.2 - Fixed a genuine gap that could make verbose logging intermittently fail to turn on Kodi's own debug logging: the code that reads and writes Kodi's core debug-logging setting only caught Python-level exceptions, never checking the actual JSON-RPC response for a rejected call - executeJSONRPC returns a valid string either way, just containing an error instead of a result when Kodi refuses the request, so a failed attempt looked identical to a successful one and got marked as done regardless, with no way to ever retry until the setting was toggled off and back on. Now checks the response properly and only marks the sync as done when Kodi's reply genuinely confirms it; a failed attempt is left unmarked so the next tick retries automatically. Confirmed via 6 direct tests covering read failures, write failures, and successful retries after each, in both directions (turning debug logging on and restoring it back off)
1.3.1 - Fixed a genuine, long-standing bug confirmed via a real log with an independent cross-check: Kodi's own player-open events showed the correct PiP target genuinely being resolved and opened, but this addon's own resolve function returned the MAIN stream's own URL instead, causing that same channel to play in both windows whenever the two genuinely differed. Root cause: Kodi's Player callbacks fire globally for any playback event, not just playback the specific instance itself started - the object tracking the PiP target's resolve stayed alive through the whole function, including the point later on where the main stream gets resumed via a separate call, which also fires the same callback and silently overwrote the already-correct value with the main stream's own URL right before it was used to launch mpv. Now only the first firing is ever accepted, so a later, unrelated playback event can no longer clobber it. This also means a previous conclusion, given in this conversation, that a user had selected the same channel for both main and PiP was wrong - that conclusion trusted this addon's own logging as ground truth without realising the very value being logged had already been corrupted by this bug before being printed
1.3.0 Picture-in-Picture for The Loop, via mpv.
Windows: mpv runs as a real floating window with full control from the context menu at any time - move, resize, swap main/PiP, swap audio independently, close. If mpv isn't found, offers to download and auto-install it (bundled 7zr.exe, falls back to a system 7-Zip install if present). Corner-anchored resize keeps the PiP flush against whichever screen corner is selected, following the real playing video's actual aspect ratio rather than a fixed shape.
Android / Fire TV: hands the stream to mpv-android or mpvNova via an Android Intent - no move/resize/swap/close control is possible there, by design, since Android sandboxes apps from one another. A "Download mpv for Android" menu item fetches the latest APK for whichever variant is selected in settings and updates the package name to match automatically.
Resolving a stream tries a direct, non-interrupting method first; where that isn't available, a fallback briefly interrupts the main stream while resolving, with a visible progress dialog and a working Cancel button, then resumes it automatically - reporting honestly if that resume genuinely fails, rather than guessing at a recovery that could play the wrong content.
The background service self-heals if mpv exits unexpectedly (a dead stream, network failure) rather than leaving the main stream stuck behind an empty window, and cleans up any orphaned mpv process on startup or shutdown.
Diagnostics category in settings: verbose logging for full launch arguments, per-step positioning, and install/download detail, which also syncs Kodi's own core debug logging on and off to match without needing to enable it separately - restoring it to whatever it was before if it was already on for another reason.
Fixed in this version: a crash on Android present since the very first version, confirmed via a real user's traceback - accessing a Windows-only API unconditionally at import time took down the entire addon, including the background service, before any platform check ever ran. Every function now checks the platform correctly and returns a safe default when this addon's OS-level window control genuinely isn't applicable, instead of crashing.
Not currently supported: RedLight and Mad Titan Sports were briefly added and then removed after confirming, via direct testing, that combining multiple addons in the context menu's visibility check broke it entirely, regardless of how that check was structured - a problem worth solving properly and separately, not bundled with keeping the addon working.
